title: Casper and the Crown
premise: When the Thornfell border wards collapse and every star in the sky goes dark, cartographer Vesper Vane discovers the two disasters are one: the crown of the sleeping King Aldric has become a parasite, feeding on starlight and memory to keep itself alive. Guided by a smuggler's map that rewrites itself as they travel, Vesper must reach the moonlit citadel before the thirteenth turn of the moon, when the crown will finish devouring the king and turn its hunger on the realm. Along the way Vesper learns their own memories have been edited — that they once served the crown and fled, and the price of unbinding the king is reclaiming what they chose to forget. In the end, Vester unbinds the crown not by destroying it but by giving it a new memory to hold, freeing Aldric at the cost of their own mapped past, and the stars return one by one as Vesper begins drawing a map of a self they no longer remember.
about_author: Rafael Pemberton is a former surveyor who spent a decade charting mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. They write in the margins of old maps and claim every novel begins as a route they never took.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Working late on a smuggler's chart of the Thornfell passes, Vesper watches every star extinguish at once and feels the border wards snap like cut rope. Refugees flood the valley road. The emotional beat is quiet dread: a professional knows when a map — and a world — has stopped making sense.

chapters.title: A Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Fleeing with the refugees, Vesper finds their old maps redrawing themselves overnight, ink crawling into new routes. A dying ward-keeper presses a broken compass into their hands, whispering that the crown eats what it cannot hold. Beat: reluctant responsibility; Vesper decides to climb toward the citadel rather than run.

chapters.title: The King in the Dark
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV, dreamlike and fragmented. Inside the citadel, the sleeping king drifts through his own eroding memories, unable to recall his mother's face but remembering taxes with perfect clarity. Something cold and patient speaks to him from the crown. Beat: tragic intimacy — we meet the victim before the quest meets the villain.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the pass town of Hollowmere, Vesper barges passage with Brannic, a smuggler who owes them a debt and trusts them less. The moon has begun its first turn, marked by frost that grows in rings. Beat: uneasy alliance; humor against encroaching fear.

chapters.title: What the Compass Points To
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The broken compass doesn't point north — it points to memories, tugging toward Vesper's own past. When it spins wildly near a shrine, Vesper suffers their first flashback: hands in white gloves, an oath they cannot place. Beat: the mystery turns inward.

chapters.title: The Crown's Servants
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Crown-sworn hunters in starless armor raid Hollowmere, collecting 'unmapped' people — those the crown cannot predict. Brannic watches Vesper's name on their list and realizes his passenger is the prize. Beat: betrayal-adjacent tension; Brannic chooses, for now, loyalty over coin.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A hermit cartographer, Old Sable, explains the mechanics: the crown was forged to hold the realm's memories safe, and it has turned predator, consuming the king to survive the starless dark. The moon's thirteenth turn completes the devouring. Beat: stakes clarified; the quest gains a clock and a rule.

chapters.title: The Map That Lies
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper's self-rewriting map leads them into a crown ambush; Brannic is captured covering their escape. Vesper realizes the map isn't helping them — it's herding them. Beat: despair and self-doubt; the tools of their identity have been compromised.

chapters.title: Cells Without Windows
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. In the crown's dungeon, Brannic meets prisoners who have forgotten their own names, and a jailer who remembers everything for them — and grieves it. Brannic trades information for Vesper's life. Beat: moral compromise; the cost of loyalty becomes concrete.

chapters.title: The Oath in White Gloves
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, intercut with flashbacks. The compass drags Vesper to a ruined observatory where the full memory surfaces: they were once the crown's Cartographer Royal, and they mapped the routes by which it feeds. Beat: identity shatters — the hero was the architect of the harm.

chapters.title: Aldric Wakes, Briefly
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. A crack in the crown's hold lets Aldric surface for one hour. He leaves a message stitched into starlight for whoever is climbing toward him: don't save me, unbind me. Beat: fragile hope; victim becomes collaborator.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Road
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper breaks Brannic out using a smuggler's route only the crown's former cartographer would know — proof their past self is useful even now. The moon completes its fourth turn. Beat: reclaiming competence; partnership deepens into trust.

chapters.title: The Jailer's Grief
chapters.summary: The jailer's POV. The man who remembers for the forgotten prisoners confronts Vesper, begging to be freed from a memory he never chose to carry. Vesper refuses — then regrets it. Beat: the theme made flesh; memory as burden and gift, power corrupting even its custodians.

chapters.title: Frost Rings and False Kings
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The crown sends an impostor — a memory-perfect copy of Vesper's dead mentor — to turn them back. Vesper sees through it because the false mentor is kind, and the real one never was. Beat: grief weaponized and survived; Vesper hardens.

chapters.title: The Citadel Below the Moon
chapters.summary: Vesper and Brannic's POV, alternating. They reach the citadel's outer walls as the moon's ninth turn freezes the valley. The stars are not dead, Sable's notes reveal — the crown is hoarding them inside itself. Beat: awe and horror; the scale of the theft becomes visible.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wants
chapters.summary: The crown's POV, cold and vast. It speaks to Vesper directly: it does not want a king, it wants a cartographer — someone to map an infinite hunger. It offers Vesper their erased memories back, whole, in exchange for service. Beat: the temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: Brannic's Price
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Brannic learns the crown will release every prisoner it holds — including the nameless — if Vesper accepts. He tells Vesper to take the deal. Vesper refuses. Beat: the friendship fractures under the weight of sacrifice; the lowest point before the climb.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the throne room, Vesper reaches the sleeping king and understands the truth Sable hinted at: a crown binds by holding memory, so it can only be unbound by being given a memory it must keep forever. Beat: the plan crystallizes; resolve replaces fear.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Vesper and Aldric's POV, braided. As the moon completes its final turn, Vesper offers the crown their reclaimed past — every memory, including their guilt — as its eternal holding. The crown accepts. Aldric wakes. Beat: the climax; identity traded for a kingdom's freedom.

chapters.title: Stars, Returning
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The hoarded stars spill back into the sky one by one. Aldric, alive and hollowed, kneels to the cartographer who cannot remember why they came. Beat: catharsis and cost held together; the realm breathes again.

chapters.title: A Map of No One
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Awake but erased, Vesper finds their own handwriting in the margins of an old chart and cannot read the person who wrote it. Brannic stays anyway. Beat: bittersweet quiet; identity as something drawn anew rather than recovered.

chapters.title: The First New Road
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Months later, Vester draws the first line of a new map — not of realms, but of the life they are rebuilding — while Aldric, crowned in plain iron, watches the stars hold. Beat: hopeful resolution; power bounded, memory chosen, identity begun again.
